items.title: Coastal Risk Engineer
items.summary: Built and validated a long-term shoreline-evolution model for one of France's most exposed tourist coastlines, projecting retreat at Lacanau (5 km) to 2100 under multiple sea-level-rise scenarios.
bullets: Problem — Lacanau's beachfront needed defensible long-term erosion projections to support coastal-risk planning under sea-level rise.

Approach — Developed the coupled LX-ST model, integrating cross-shore (ShoreTrans) and longshore sediment transport, and ran SSP2-4.5, SSP5-8.5, and High-End climate scenarios with sensitivity testing.
Deliverable — A validated, peer-reviewed shoreline-evolution model applied to the 5 km Lacanau site, with erosion-rate sensitivity bands for planning.
Evidence — Published in Environmental Modelling & Software (2025); method and results are peer-reviewed.

items.title: Numerical Modeling of Coastline & Sandy Beaches under Sea-Level Rise
items.summary: Turned a MATLAB research model (ShoreTrans) into fast, portable Fortran engineering software, adding 2D capability for real coastal geometries.
bullets: Problem — The published ShoreTrans model (McCarroll et al., 2021) ran in MATLAB, was slow for repeated engineering-scale runs, and lacked 2D capability for complex coastlines.
Approach — Enhanced BRGM's LX-Shore code with a Fortran ShoreTrans module, adding 2D modeling capability and refined sediment-transport algorithms.
Deliverable — A faster, portable shoreline-evolution codebase, validated against observed coastal-evolution data.
Evidence — Open-sourced as ShoreTrans-fortran; see the repository for the full implementation.

items.title: Impact of Climate Change on Gironde Estuary Hydrodynamics
items.summary: Stress-tested France's largest estuary against climate change, modeling flood and drought scenarios to 2100 for the Gironde and its Garonne and Dordogne tributaries.
bullets: Problem — The Gironde estuary, France's largest, needed a hydrodynamic assessment of climate-driven flood and drought risk, including dredging impacts on circulation.
Approach — Built coupled Telemac2D/Telemac3D models of the estuary and its Garonne and Dordogne tributaries, running climate-scenario projections to 2100.
Deliverable — A validated hydrodynamic model quantifying dredging impacts and long-term circulation change.
Evidence — Findings contributed to French national climate-adaptation strategy and were published in JNGCGC (2022).
